settings.title: They keep circling after they've lain down.
settings.text: A couple of turns before settling is just what dogs do. Turning, resettling, then shifting again ten minutes later usually means no position on that bed takes the weight off.

settings.title: They've started choosing the floor.
settings.text: Once foam has bottomed out, cold tiles genuinely are the firmer, flatter option. A dog picking the kitchen floor over their own bed has done the comparison and reached a conclusion.

settings.title: There's a dip that doesn't spring back.
settings.text: Press a flat hand into the middle where they lie. If you can feel the floor through it, so can their hips and elbows.

settings.heading: Three signs their bed has stopped working.
settings.lede: None of this is anyone's fault. Beds wear out quietly, and dogs don't complain. Here's what to look for tonight.
settings.note: A bed can't undo ageing. What it can change is how much effort goes into lying down, and how much goes into getting back up.

settings.title: Curled in a ball
settings.text: Nose tucked under the tail, back pressed into something.

settings.title: Head on something
settings.text: Chin on the sofa arm, a cushion, a wall, or you.

settings.title: Stretched flat out
settings.text: On their side, legs at full stretch, taking the whole bed.

settings.heading: How does your dog sleep?
settings.lede: Think of how you find them at 2am, not how they settle at 9pm. Tap the closest, and we'll take it from there.

settings.question: How do I know which size to get?
settings.answer: Measure nose to base of tail while they're lying down, then add about 20cm. Between two sizes? Go up. Every bed's page lists the sleeping area, and the size guide has breed examples. Still unsure? Send us their breed and weight and we'll tell you honestly which size fits.

settings.question: What's inside, and isn't firmer better?
settings.answer: It depends on the bed, so each page says exactly what's inside: memory foam, egg-crate foam, crumb memory foam, fibre or mesh. Firmness is only how a bed feels on day one. What matters is whether it holds its shape in month six, which is why the orthopaedic beds are built on foam rather than loose filling. What's inside our beds explains each one.

settings.question: What if my dog just won't use it?
settings.answer: Then it comes back. Some dogs claim a new bed the first night; some take a fortnight. Put it where they already sleep, with a blanket that smells of home on top. If after that it still isn't right, tell us any time inside the [nights] nights and we collect it free from the UK mainland and refund every penny.

settings.question: Will it help a dog with arthritis or stiff hips?
settings.answer: A supportive bed spreads their weight so pressure isn't concentrated on hips, elbows and shoulders, and a low front means stepping in rather than climbing over. But a bed is for comfort, not a treatment, and it won't replace veterinary care. Please keep talking to your vet. Our beds for older dogs and the senior sleep guide go further.

settings.question: When will it arrive, and what does delivery cost?

Every product page shows the dates for an order placed today. A few beds ship from our partner warehouse and take longer; their pages say so before you order.

settings.question: Can I actually wash it?
settings.answer: On most of the range the cover comes off and washes, following the care label sewn into it. Beds with a coated, waterproof cover are wiped clean instead. Foam is never machine washed. The care guide covers covers, liners and the smell that creeps in by February.
